reviews.explanation: The mention 温嶠 appears in the Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-003) as 平南温嶠 who sends a 叅軍 upon hearing of the rebellion. The candidate evidence from people.json provides the canonical name 温嶠. The annotation explicitly names 温嶠 with the title 平南, and the main text's 温公 (sfh1-mention-85cf555406104fdc819bb08b) is the same person who advises 庾亮. The identity is directly supported by the source text naming 温嶠 explicitly.

The mention 庾公 in the main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-main) refers to 庾亮, who is the subject of the story about being pursued by 陶侃. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-001) explicitly states 令庾亮以元舅輔政, confirming 庾公 = 庾亮. The alias evidence from aliases.json provides 庾公 as a contextual title for 庾亮. The main text context — 陶公欲誅庾公, 温公勸庾詣陶, 庾元規何縁拜陶士衡 — all consistently identify 庾公 as 庾亮 (庾元規).

The mention 温公 in the main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-main) refers to the person who advises 庾亮 to go see 陶侃. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-003) explicitly names 平南温嶠 as the one who sends a 叅軍 upon hearing of the rebellion — this is the same person as 温公 in the main text. The alias evidence from aliases.json provides 温公 as a contextual title for 温嶠. The story context (温公勸庾詣陶) aligns with 温嶠's historical role as mediator between 庾亮 and 陶侃.

The mention 陶侃 is the canonical name directly matching the candidate. The main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-main) refers to 陶公 who comes from upstream to punish 庾公, and the Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-004) explicitly names 征西陶侃 as the one pushed to be盟主. The main text also has 陶士衡 (陶侃's courtesy name) confirming the identity. The candidate evidence from people.json provides the canonical name 陶侃. This is a direct name match with strong source grounding.

The mention surface is 蘇峻, which exactly matches the canonical name of the candidate. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-002) explicitly discusses 蘇峻 as a rebel figure (豺狼) in the context of the Su Jun rebellion, consistent with the historical Su Jun. The main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-main) also references 蘇峻之難 (the Su Jun disaster), confirming this is the historical rebel general Su Jun. The direct name match plus contextual corroboration from the annotation text supports the identity resolution.

The mention surface is 我 (first-person pronoun). The main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-main) shows 温公勸庾詣陶曰...我為卿保之 — the speaker saying 'I will guarantee it for you' is 温公, who is identified as 温嶠. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-003) explicitly names 平南温嶠 in the same narrative context. The speaker role and coreference chain to 温公/温嶠 are clearly established by the supplied evidence.

The mention surface is 亮 (surname-only reference). The main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-main) shows 庾元規 (Yu Yuan-gui, i.e., 庾亮) being addressed, and the narrative concerns 庾公/庾亮 throughout. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-004) states 時亮敗績, referring to 庾亮's defeat, which matches the main text context where 庾 suffered defeat. The surname-only form 亮 is a standard abbreviated reference to 庾亮, and the contextual identification is strongly supported by the supplied evidence.

The mention surface is 蘇峻, exactly matching the canonical name of the candidate. The main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-main) opens with 陶公自上流來赴蘇峻之難, referring to the Su Jun rebellion. The Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-002) explicitly discusses 蘇峻 as the rebel figure. Although the semantic record for this mention returned 'uncertain' (fail closed), the supplied evidence directly names 蘇峻 in the same historical context, and the exact name match with the candidate's canonical name provides sufficient support for identity.

陶士衡 is the courtesy name of 陶侃. The main text has 陶公 referring to the same person, and the annotation sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-004 explicitly mentions 征西陶侃 in the same narrative context (the Su Jun rebellion). The speech '庾元規何縁拜陶士衡' has 陶侃 referring to himself by his courtesy name. The evidence directly supports this identity.

嶠 is the personal name of 温嶠. The annotation sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-004 explicitly names 温嶠 in the same narrative context, and the text '嶠愈相崇重分兵以配給之' describes 温嶠's actions toward 庾亮. The mention is a local anaphoric reference to the previously named 温嶠. The evidence directly supports this identity.

庾亮 is the canonical name matching the surface form exactly. The annotation sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-003 explicitly names 庾亮 in the context of the Su Jun rebellion narrative, and the main text's 庾公/庾 refers to the same person. The annotation evidence directly supports this identity.

庾元規 is the courtesy name of 庾亮. The main text has 陶侃 addressing 庾亮 by this courtesy name in the speech '庾元規何縁拜陶士衡'. The annotation sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-003 explicitly names 庾亮 in the same narrative context. The evidence directly supports this identity.

The mention 王導 appears in the Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-002) alongside 卞壷 as both advising against summoning Su Jun. The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-5ce98994f4070dc10b7c) provides the canonical name 王導 from people.json. The full-name form 王導 in the annotation context of advising against summoning Su Jun matches the historical Wang Dao, the Eastern Jin statesman. The annotation explicitly names 王導 and 卞壷 together in the same advisory role, which is consistent with the historical record. No contradicting evidence exists.

The mention 陶公 appears in the main text (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-main) where 陶公 comes from upstream to respond to Su Jun's rebellion and orders the execution of 庾公. The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-e722703aa51200461f0d) from aliases.json explicitly identifies 陶公 as 陶侃, and the text later refers to 陶士衡 (Tao Kan's courtesy name), confirming the identity. The honorific 公 with the surname 陶, combined with the explicit 陶士衡 reference in the same passage, unambiguously identifies this as 陶侃. The coreference with the full name 陶侃 in the annotation is supported.

The mention 庾亮 appears in the Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-27-jiajue-008-liu-annotation-001) which states 令庾亮以元舅輔政 (ordered Yu Liang as chief maternal uncle to assist in governance). The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-ce132e3fa4c077c75300) provides the canonical name 庾亮 from people.json. The annotation explicitly names 庾亮 and describes his role as 元舅輔政 during 成帝's infancy with 太后 presiding over court, which precisely matches the historical Yu Liang. The full-name form in the annotation directly supports the identity resolution.
